c.tagline: Canada's capital of grand museums, canal skating, and tulip-lined riverbanks.

taxi.fareNote: Metered cabs from Capital Taxi and Blue Line are common at the airport and downtown; Uber and Lyft also operate throughout the city.

emergency.note: 911 is the single emergency number for police, fire, and ambulance across Canada.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.The Glebe: The Glebe Bank Street Ottawa Lansdowne

avoid.reason: The ByWard Market blocks get rowdy after bar close, with some visible drug activity; keep usual late-night awareness.

hood_desc: Ottawa's oldest and liveliest quarter, a walkable maze of the historic farmers' market, pubs, restaurants, and nightlife just east of Parliament; the top pick for visitors who want to eat, drink, and stay in the thick of it.
The government and business core around Parliament Hill, the Rideau Canal, and Sparks Street, dense with hotels, museums, and offices; a central, convenient base for first-time sightseeing.

A leafy, upscale residential neighborhood along Bank Street south of downtown, known for indie boutiques, cafes, Lansdowne Park, and the canal; relaxed and stylish, good for shopping and a local feel.

A quiet, historic residential area east of downtown around the University of Ottawa, full of heritage homes, embassies, and Strathcona Park; calm and walkable, popular with students and budget travelers.
A trendy west-end village of design shops, brunch spots, outdoor-gear stores, and beach access on the Ottawa River; a laid-back, health-conscious enclave with an indie, hipster streak.
lodging: Days Inn by Wyndham Ottawa West

water.note: Tap water is safe and high quality.

transit.pay: Tap a Presto card or a contactless credit/debit card, or use an OC Transpo mobile ticket, at O-Train gates and on buses. An adult single ride is C$4.10 and covers 90 minutes of transfers; Presto daily fares are capped at C$12.25.
transit.hours: O-Train and most bus routes run roughly 5am to 1am, with a limited overnight bus network filling the late-night gap.

bus: Ottawa Central Station (FlixBus / Megabus intercity to Toronto, Montreal, Kingston)

transit.m: O-Train Line 4 (Airport Link) to Bayview, then Line 1 to downtown (~35 min)

tip.r: ~15-20% is customary at restaurants and bars; $1-2 per drink and a few dollars for taxis and rideshares.

food.name: BeaverTails
food.desc: Ottawa-born fried dough stretched into a beaver-tail shape and topped with cinnamon sugar, maple butter or the chocolate-hazelnut Killaloe.

places.name: BeaverTails ByWard Market
places.note: The original 1978 pastry shack on George Street; still the busiest counter in town.

places.name: Rideau Canal Skateway huts
places.note: Winter-only shacks on the ice - the way locals actually eat one.

places.name: BeaverTails Sparks Street
places.note: Downtown pedestrian mall branch, handy between Parliament and the canal.

food.name: Ottawa shawarma
food.desc: Ottawa has an unusually deep Lebanese shawarma scene: garlic-heavy toum, pickled turnip and shaved chicken or beef in a pressed wrap.

places.name: Shawarma Palace
places.note: The city's benchmark shawarma, open late and repeatedly voted best in Ottawa.

places.name: Three Brothers Shawarma
places.note: Longtime rival on the Glebe end of Bank; huge portions, strong garlic sauce.

places.name: Shawarma joints on Rideau Street
places.note: A dense strip of late-night shops serving the ByWard bar crowd.

food.name: Poutine
food.desc: Fries, squeaky Quebec cheese curds and hot gravy - eaten here at all hours, often loaded with smoked meat, pulled pork or peppercorn gravy.

places.name: Elgin Street Diner
places.note: Open 24 hours; the classic Ottawa post-night-out poutine.

places.name: Zak's Diner
places.note: Retro all-night diner in the market with a long poutine list.

places.name: Chip trucks on Sparks Street
places.note: Ottawa's summer chip wagons do fresh-cut fries and gravy at lunch.

food.name: Maple syrup treats
food.desc: Maple taffy poured on snow, maple butter tarts, maple candy and pancakes drenched in Ontario syrup - a spring sugar-shack tradition.

places.name: Canadian Maple Delights
places.note: Market shop for syrup grades, maple gelato and maple pastry year-round.

places.name: Fulton's Pancake House and Sugar Bush
places.note: Working sugar bush an hour out; taffy on snow during the March-April run.

places.name: Proulx Maple and Berry Farm
places.note: Family farm east of Ottawa doing sugar-shack meals in spring.

food.name: Obama cookie and ByWard bakes
food.desc: The maple-leaf shortbread Barack Obama bought in 2009, plus butter tarts and Nanaimo bars from the market's bakery counters.

places.name: Le Moulin de Provence
places.note: The bakery that made the cookie famous; still labelled the Obama cookie.

places.name: ByWard Market Building stalls
places.note: Indoor market counters selling butter tarts and Canadian classics.

places.name: Farmers stalls on ByWard Market Square
places.note: Seasonal Ottawa Valley produce, cider doughnuts and preserves.

food.name: Montreal-style bagels and smoked meat
food.desc: Wood-fired, honey-boiled bagels and hand-carved smoked-meat sandwiches on rye with mustard - Ottawa's take on its neighbour's classics.

places.name: Kettleman's Bagel Co.
places.note: Ottawa institution baking in a wood oven around the clock.

places.name: Nate's Deli
places.note: Long-running Jewish deli name in Ottawa for smoked meat on rye.

places.name: ByWard Market delis
places.note: Several market counters carve smoked meat to order at lunch.

food.name: Ottawa Valley craft beer
food.desc: A strong local brewing scene: Ottawa Valley pale ales, lagers and sours poured in neighbourhood taprooms across Hintonburg and Little Italy.

places.name: Beyond the Pale Brewing
places.note: One of Ottawa's original craft breweries with a big industrial taproom.

places.name: Dominion City Brewing
places.note: Award-winning local brewer with a taproom pouring fresh small batches.

places.name: Flora Hall Brewing
places.note: Brewpub with a full kitchen, handy to Elgin Street and the canal.

food.name: Caesar cocktail
food.desc: Canada's national cocktail: vodka, spiced Clamato, Worcestershire and hot sauce on a celery-salt rim, garnished to excess on brunch menus.

places.name: Metropolitain Brasserie
places.note: Parisian-style brasserie by the National Gallery, good for a brunch Caesar.

places.name: The Lieutenant's Pump
places.note: Neighbourhood pub that has poured Caesars on Elgin for decades.

places.name: Elgin Street Diner
places.note: Round-the-clock diner where the Caesar comes loaded.

landmarks: Parliament Hill & Centre Block
The neo-Gothic seat of Canada's federal government, crowned by the iconic Peace Tower, is the nation's most photographed landmark.
Rideau Canal
A UNESCO World Heritage waterway that becomes the world's largest skating rink in winter and a scenic boating route in summer.
Château Laurier
A castle-like grand railway hotel of copper-roofed turrets that dominates Ottawa's skyline near Parliament Hill.
ByWard Market
One of Canada's oldest and largest public markets, alive with food stalls, boutiques, and street performers.
Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica
Ottawa's oldest and largest church, notable for its twin silver spires and richly decorated Gothic Revival interior.
National Gallery of Canada & Maman Spider Sculpture
A glass-and-granite art museum famous for the giant bronze spider sculpture standing guard outside.
National War Memorial, Confederation Square
A soaring bronze-and-granite arch honoring Canada's war dead, set in the ceremonial heart of the capital.
Rideau Hall
The stately official residence of Canada's Governor General, set on expansive landscaped grounds open to visitors.
Canadian Museum of History
A sweeping, wave-like building across the river in Gatineau offering a striking view back toward Parliament Hill.
Major's Hill Park
A scenic riverside park with unbeatable photo vantage points of Parliament Hill, the canal locks, and Château Laurier.

train.note: No international trains from Ottawa - the cross-border Amtrak Adirondack to New York departs from Montreal. VIA Rail's Corridor services from Ottawa station reach Montreal in about 2 hours and Toronto in 4h30, with several departures a day. The station is southeast of downtown on the O-Train Line 1. VIA's Escape fares are much cheaper if booked well ahead.

bus.note: No direct international coaches - for New York or Boston you connect in Montreal. Since Greyhound Canada closed, the Ottawa market is served by Megabus (https://ca.megabus.com/), Rider Express (https://riderexpress.ca/) and FlixBus (https://www.flixbus.ca/) running to Toronto in about 5 hours and Montreal in 2h15, from the station area rather than a single central terminal - check your ticket for the pickup point.

ferry.note: There is no scheduled passenger ferry in Ottawa. Sightseeing boats run on the Ottawa River and the Rideau Canal in summer, and the canal freezes into the Rideau Canal Skateway in winter. The nearest working car ferry crosses the river to Quebec at Cumberland-Masson, east of the city.

half.name: Gatineau Park
half.blurb: Forested hiking trails and fall-foliage lookouts across the river in Quebec are about twenty minutes from downtown Ottawa.

half.name: Wakefield
half.blurb: A riverside Quebec village with a covered bridge and a steam train lies roughly forty minutes north of Ottawa.

half.name: Merrickville
half.blurb: A stone-mill village on the Rideau Canal with antique shops sits about an hour south of Ottawa.

half.name: Kingston
half.blurb: Fort Henry and the Thousand Islands gateway on Lake Ontario are roughly two hours southwest of Ottawa.

full.name: Montreal
full.blurb: Quebec's largest city, with Old Montreal's cobblestone streets and Notre-Dame Basilica, is about two hours east of Ottawa.
